package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package, but rather discusses industry-wide vulnerability trends, remediation times, and the prevalence of certain vulnerability types in retail and hospitality applications.

behavioral_signatures: Exploitation of web vulnerabilities such as improper access control, information disclosure, and cross-site scripting (XSS)
Targeting of large, frequently updated attack surfaces (e.g., retail and hospitality platforms with many web properties)
Replication of attack methods across similar sites within the same industry
file_indicators: Web application files with improper access control logic
Pages or scripts vulnerable to XSS (e.g., user input reflected in HTML/JS without sanitization)
Endpoints leaking sensitive information (e.g., customer data, loyalty program details)
network_indicators: Unusual POST/GET requests exploiting authentication or authorization flaws
Requests containing XSS payloads or attempts to access unauthorized resources
Patterns of automated scanning or repeated access to similar endpoints across multiple retail/hospitality domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for common web vulnerability exploitation patterns, such as repeated failed access attempts, injection payloads in requests, and access to sensitive endpoints without proper authentication. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to detect and block XSS and IDOR attempts. Regularly review logs for information disclosure incidents and implement automated scanning for known vulnerability types across all web properties, especially after mergers or system refreshes.
